LESSON: MODELLING AND ORNAMENT MAKING.

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.6: Modelling and Ornament Making.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Modelling and Ornament Making., part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are ornaments made?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify modelled beads for familiarity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. model beads using pellet technique,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. decorate the beads

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. make a beaded ornament,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appraise own and others modelled items for appreciation.  Learners to explore virtual and actual samples of beaded ornaments. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.  In purposive groups, learners to roll clay/ papier mache to make pellets for beading. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.  Learners to pierce the pellets to make a hole through for stringing and leave them to dry under shade. How are ornaments made? 35  Learners to decorate the beads by painting. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted panting tools and materials.  Learners to pass string to make a single stranded necklace. Learners with manipulation difficulties could be supported  Learners to display the ornament for peers feedback. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Modelling and Ornament Making. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication and collaboration: as the learner work together prepare clay or papier mache for modelling items

 Creativity and imagination: as the learner creates make a single stranded necklace and a matching bracelet,

Values:
 Respect: is promoted as the learner gives positive feedback as they display items made.

 Unity: is enhanced as the learner in groups, prepare clay or papier mache for modelling items.

 Patriotism: is promoted as the learner takes pride in making ornaments using recyclable materials from the local

community.

36

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
 Safety and security: The learner observes their safety as they fire the clay beads in an improvised kiln.

 Social cohesion: The learner portrays team spirit as they explore pinch and pellet technique to make simple forms in pairs.

Link to other subjects:

Environmental Activities: as the learner applies knowledge and skills gained in Environmental Activities to create melodic

patterns from differently pitched objects such as voiced or tuned percussion.

Suggested learning resources:

Relevant virtual sites, pictures, reference books, flash cards, digital devices, clay/ papier mache, assistive technology such as

universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input

devices such as head wand
